title: The black hours
author: lyvondroa
selftext:
This is 2 weeks of my project. Inspired by bloodborne and the like. Graphically inspired by 2D HD games like octopath traveler and the sort. Any ideas are welcome, or animation fixes from the small prototype trailer you think will be of any benefit regarding the 2D HD look. 

The black hours is a vampire survivors rogue like that is built around Gothic horror and the divine office. Vesper, laudes, and compline. (5 more characters to be introduced) so far, I have 15 weapons designed up to 59 with combinations. Bosses have a unique death animation. The deeper you dive into the world, and the longer you stay the more uneasy the playable characters become. After waking from a nightmare, NPC's will be performing surgery to keep you alive. At the moment they scatter, they're afraid. They run. Hiding under tables, or scurrying to the roof. The more you fail, the more NPC's start to get frantic, and uneasy about your ability to save the church. Somewhat like a hidden stress meter. At the moment they don't change anything, just get.. More creepy.. Enemies are of multiply variety, each with different attacks.

comments.author: Beartrox
comments.body: what did you use for character creation and animation if you don't mind me asking?

replies.author: lyvondroa
replies.body:
This will be a bit long. But I hope it helps. 

Claude code opus 5.5 on extra with a mix of fable for ideas. Fable wasn't really needed though, honestly it failed me more times then helped. Pixellab with claude code MCP too. I tried using blender and it uh... Never ended up well I think I spent roughly 50 hours, and it came out terrible with animations everytime no matter how tight the prompt. However, Claude code has used a ton of python.CS to put the harshly drawn lines. The maps, and assets are drawn with Python.CS with claude code. But I had to provide it a very strict prompt about how it should look in the 2D HD style with Gothic horror. Pixellab it creates the sprite, and animations. NPC's are provided via Claude using python. The finisher you see on the boss was also done by Claude with each iteration a different prompt frame by frame. Once it created the concept I had it make an artifact for review before implementation. Took my past game knowledge and had it work to what I thought looked best. Now, grok is also good at this for ideas and frame by frame mp4 analysis to help provide even tighter prompts. Since there's blood, grok doesn't care about uncensored things. Claude does. So it helps fine tune, to not trip specific Claude code protocol.

replies.author: lyvondroa
replies.body:
Oh wow that's funny! Ill try to be as in depth and short as I can. But, tried I tried 3D as well and it uh... I couldn't. Lmao I swapped from unity to unreal, had a ton of issues with everything and swapped back to unity and kept the 2D HD. But, my work flow for the most part is

1. Design the character in pixellab as best you can. With simple design so you don't blow your credits. In a 64 format. Once your happy with the design. I used pixellab character creator in the low top down aspect since it matches the game.

2. I passed it to Claude and asked it to provide animation to it via MCP on pixellab in all 8 directions. Idle, movement, dashing, lunging, and walking, are each a different frame with a "phantom image" so it doesn't look blunt when say you dash, to an idle animation. This keeps the smoothness without anyone noticing since it happens so quickly. If any flickers happen, it's fixed in pixellab's skeleton mode which holds the sprite steady. (also done by Claude code) for example, if I notice anything off I'll screenshot it up close on the exact frame and let Claude know. It'll make a 64x64 grid automatically and tweak it.

3. I have Claude provide something called a smoke test and an automated play test and watch it. I'm only 1 person, so seeing things from different perspectives is difficult. People will play different then me, so it provides me a good "watch and see what's incorrect" in terms of pixel "anatomy" if you will. This happens every small update. Slightly annoying since it insists on repacking the zip for a play test build but it helps a ton.

Since there is an idle animation attack, I have the walking or dashing override it with a similar frame that it should be on to keep it smooth. This was the difficult part. Really difficult. Without making the character seem like it's "clipping" I hope this helps at least a bit!

TLDR: The characters are made as 8-direction pixel art in PixelLab from the design, cleaned up frame by frame with custom scripts, packed into sprite sheets by a Unity tool, and drawn as lit sprites in a 3D world, HD-2D style.
